photoobj_basic.name: photoobj_basic
photoobj_basic.body_sql:
SELECT
  objid,
  run,
  rerun,
  field,
  mode,
  type,
  clean,
  flags,
  rowc,
  colc,
  cmodelmag_u,
  cmodelmag_g,
  cmodelmag_r,
  ra,
  dec,
  b,
  l,
  extinction_r,
  mjd,
  loadversion,
  u,
  g,
  r,
  i,
  z
FROM photoobj

params.description: Provides one-row-per-object photometric and positional basic attributes for objects in the photoobj table (objid-grain).
params.when_to_use: Retrieve basic photometry (u/g/r/i/z and cmodel magnitudes) and positions for a single object or set of objects by objid. | Filter or join on object-level attributes such as run, field, clean flag, mode, type, or spatial coordinates (ra/dec/b/l). | Build higher-level queries that aggregate or cross-match object-level measurements (e.g., counts, averages) starting from a stable one-row-per-objid base.
params.output_schema: objid: unique object identifier (derived directly from photoobj.objid) | run: imaging run identifier (derived directly from photoobj.run) | rerun: processing rerun identifier/version (derived directly from photoobj.rerun) | field: imaging field number (derived directly from photoobj.field) | mode: survey mode flag/column (derived directly from photoobj.mode) | type: object type code (derived directly from photoobj.type) | clean: boolean/flag indicating clean photometry (derived directly from photoobj.clean) | flags: bitmask of processing flags for the object (derived directly from photoobj.flags) | rowc: CCD row coordinate or derived row centroid (derived directly from photoobj.rowc) | colc: CCD column coordinate or derived column centroid (derived directly from photoobj.colc) | cmodelmag_u: cmodel magnitude in u band (derived directly from photoobj.cmodelmag_u) | cmodelmag_g: cmodel magnitude in g band (derived directly from photoobj.cmodelmag_g) | cmodelmag_r: cmodel magnitude in r band (derived directly from photoobj.cmodelmag_r) | ra: right ascension in degrees (derived directly from photoobj.ra) | dec: declination in degrees (derived directly from photoobj.dec) | b: Galactic latitude in degrees (derived directly from photoobj.b) | l: Galactic longitude in degrees (derived directly from photoobj.l) | extinction_r: r-band extinction (derived directly from photoobj.extinction_r) | mjd: Modified Julian Date of observation (derived directly from photoobj.mjd) | loadversion: data load/version tag (derived directly from photoobj.loadversion) | u: PSF/aperture/measure magnitude in u band (derived directly from photoobj.u) | g: PSF/aperture/measure magnitude in g band (derived directly from photoobj.g) | r: PSF/aperture/measure magnitude in r band (derived directly from photoobj.r) | i: PSF/aperture/measure magnitude in i band (derived directly from photoobj.i) | z: PSF/aperture/measure magnitude in z band (derived directly from photoobj.z)
params.grounded_columns: photoobj.objid | photoobj.run | photoobj.rerun | photoobj.field | photoobj.mode | photoobj.type | photoobj.clean | photoobj.flags | photoobj.rowc | photoobj.colc | photoobj.cmodelmag_u | photoobj.cmodelmag_g | photoobj.cmodelmag_r | photoobj.ra | photoobj.dec | photoobj.b | photoobj.l | photoobj.extinction_r | photoobj.mjd | photoobj.loadversion | photoobj.u | photoobj.g | photoobj.r | photoobj.i | photoobj.z
params.metric: This view exposes no derived aggregate metrics; all outputs are direct column projections from photoobj (derived_col = photoobj.<column> for each output column).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension/look-up tables that are one-to-one with objid (or keyed by run/field when run+field is unique) without re-aggregation. Example: join to photo_type_lookup on type to get textual type description — safe because photo_type_lookup is a lookup (one row per type) and does not multiply rows: JOIN photo_type_lookup ON photoobj_basic.type = photo_type_lookup.type. | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables (e.g., spectroscopic observations or multiple measurements per objid) without aggregation, because that will multiply this view's rows and duplicate measures. For example, do NOT directly join photoobj_basic to specobj_basic (if specobj_basic contains multiple spectra per objid) unless you explicitly aggregate specobj_basic to one row per objid (e.g., latest spectrum per objid) or you accept multiplicative expansion. | If you need to combine object-level measures with multi-row child tables, aggregate the child table to objid grain first (COUNT, MAX, AVG, EXISTS, etc.), then join that aggregated result to this view on objid so measures remain correct and not duplicated. | Joins on run/field/rerun are safe only if the join target is one-row-per-(run,field,rerun). If the target contains multiple records per run/field (for example multiple exposures or calibrations), aggregate that target first before joining. | Because photoobj_basic is strictly one-row-per-objid by construction (grain = ['objid']), planners can treat its numeric columns as atomic per-object measures; any join that preserves the one-row-per-objid cardinality (one-to-one or many-to-one into photoobj_basic) will not duplicate these measures.

photoobj_basic.description: Normalized photometric object projection exposing primary positional, magnitude, and metadata columns with a simple cleaning of magnitudes (pass-through NULLs preserved). Use this as the canonical photoobj row for joins or downstream aggregations. | Use for: Retrieve photometry for objects by spatial region; Join photometry to spectra via bestobjid; Compute color indices or magnitude-limited samples

photo_type_lookup.name: photo_type_lookup
photo_type_lookup.body_sql:
SELECT
  value,
  name,
  description
FROM photo_type

params.description: Lookup of photo type codes to their human-readable name and description (answers what a photo_type value means).
params.when_to_use: Translate or label photo_type codes in result sets (e.g., show name/description alongside photo_type value). | Join to fact/detail tables that store a photo_type value to present the label without changing cardinality. | Compose into higher-level SQL that groups or aggregates facts by photo_type label.
params.output_schema: value: the photo_type code used as the lookup key — derives from photo_type.value | name: human-readable name/label for the photo_type code — derives from photo_type.name | description: longer text describing the photo_type code — derives from photo_type.description
params.metric: value = photo_type.value | name = photo_type.name | description = photo_type.description
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to fact/detail tables (e.g., photo-containing tables) on photo_type value using photo_type.value = <fact_table>.photo_type — safe because photo_type is a lookup/dimension with one row per value so it does NOT duplicate measures when used as a dimension. | Safe to join to photoobj_basic or specobj_basic on a photo_type or value column if those tables reference a single photo_type per row; this will not multiply the rows of the lookup but the cardinality is driven by the fact table (photoobj_basic/specobj_basic). | Do NOT join this view to a one-to-many child table (a table that has multiple rows per photo_type value) and assume aggregates from the child will remain unchanged; joining a multi-row table without aggregation will multiply the lookup rows and any embedded measures. If you need measures from a one-to-many table, first aggregate those measures at the photo_type level (GROUP BY photo_type) or use DISTINCT/appropriate grouping before joining to this lookup. | Examples of safe composition patterns: 1) SELECT f.*, l.name FROM fact_table f LEFT JOIN photo_type_lookup l ON f.photo_type = l.value; 2) SELECT l.name, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM fact_table f JOIN photo_type_lookup l ON f.photo_type = l.value GROUP BY l.name. | Examples of unsafe patterns without re-aggregation: joining photo_type_lookup to a table that contains multiple rows per photo (or other entity) expecting the lookup to reduce rows — this will not happen and may inflate counts if not grouped first.

photo_type_lookup.description: Dimension table for photo type codes. Use to translate photoobj.type into human-friendly name/description when joining with photometric rows. | Use for: Map photo type codes to labels for reporting; Filter photometry by type categories by joining to this lookup

specobj_basic.name: specobj_basic
specobj_basic.body_sql:
SELECT
  specobjid,
  bestobjid,
  plateid,
  scienceprimary,
  segue2primary,
  survey,
  programname,
  mjd,
  plate,
  fiberid,
  special_target1,
  segue2_target1,
  segue2_target2,
  ancillary_target1,
  ra,
  dec,
  z,
  zerr,
  zwarning,
  class,
  subclass,
  veldisp,
  veldisperr,
  loadversion
FROM specobj

params.description: Row-level catalog of spectroscopic objects: one record per spectroscopic object (specobjid) with identification, targeting flags, survey/program metadata, sky position, redshift and quality metrics, classification, and velocity dispersion.
params.when_to_use: Look up properties (redshift, class, coordinates) for a specific spectroscopic object (by specobjid or bestobjid). | Compose analyses that need per-spectrum metadata and measured quantities (z, zerr, zwarning, class, subclass, veldisp) as a base table for further joins/filters. | Filter or group spectra by survey/programname/plate/mjd/fiberid and then join to photometric information (via photoobj_basic) for object-level analyses. | Produce catalogs of spectra for quality cuts (scienceprimary, segue2primary, zwarning) before running per-object aggregations. | Serve as the grain-level input when computing aggregated spectroscopic summaries (counts, mean z) after appropriate aggregation.
params.output_schema: specobjid: unique identifier for the spectroscopic object — derived directly from specobj.specobjid | bestobjid: identifier linking this spectrum to a best-matching object entry — derived from specobj.bestobjid | plateid: internal plate identifier for the spectroscopic observation — derived from specobj.plateid | scienceprimary: boolean/flag indicating primary science spectrum selection — derived from specobj.scienceprimary | segue2primary: flag indicating SEQUe-2 primary target status — derived from specobj.segue2primary | survey: name of survey that obtained this spectrum (string) — derived from specobj.survey | programname: program name that produced the observation — derived from specobj.programname | mjd: modified Julian date of the spectroscopic observation — derived from specobj.mjd | plate: plate number for the observation (human-facing plate) — derived from specobj.plate | fiberid: fiber identifier on the plate for this spectrum — derived from specobj.fiberid | special_target1: targeting bitmask/flag field 1 — derived from specobj.special_target1 | segue2_target1: SEQUE2 targeting bitmask/flag field 1 — derived from specobj.segue2_target1 | segue2_target2: SEQUE2 targeting bitmask/flag field 2 — derived from specobj.segue2_target2 | ancillary_target1: ancillary target bitmask/flag field 1 — derived from specobj.ancillary_target1 | ra: right ascension (deg) of the spectroscopic source — derived from specobj.ra | dec: declination (deg) of the spectroscopic source — derived from specobj.dec | z: measured redshift for this spectrum — derived from specobj.z | zerr: redshift error estimate — derived from specobj.zerr | zwarning: z-warning quality flag (non-zero indicates issues) — derived from specobj.zwarning | class: spectroscopic class label (STAR/GALAXY/QSO/etc.) — derived from specobj.class | subclass: spectroscopic subclass label (detailed classification) — derived from specobj.subclass | veldisp: velocity dispersion measurement (km/s or dataset units) — derived from specobj.veldisp | veldisperr: velocity dispersion error estimate — derived from specobj.veldisperr | loadversion: provenance/version tag indicating the pipeline/catalog load version — derived from specobj.loadversion
params.grounded_columns: specobj.specobjid | specobj.bestobjid | specobj.plateid | specobj.scienceprimary | specobj.segue2primary | specobj.survey | specobj.programname | specobj.mjd | specobj.plate | specobj.fiberid | specobj.special_target1 | specobj.segue2_target1 | specobj.segue2_target2 | specobj.ancillary_target1 | specobj.ra | specobj.dec | specobj.z | specobj.zerr | specobj.zwarning | specobj.class | specobj.subclass | specobj.veldisp | specobj.veldisperr | specobj.loadversion
params.metric: row_count = COUNT(*)  -- count of spectroscopic objects at the view grain (specobjid) | mean_z = AVG(z)  -- average redshift computed by aggregating z over the view rows (must aggregate after appropriate filtering) | count_good_z = SUM(CASE WHEN zwarning = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)  -- number of spectra with no z warnings | distinct_bestobjid = COUNT(DISTINCT bestobjid)  -- number of unique linked objects across the selected spectra
params.composition: Cardinality-SAFE joins (do not duplicate this view's measures): |  - Join to photoobj_basic on bestobjid = photoobj_basic.bestobjid (one-to-one or many-to-one from specobj to photoobj_basic depending on photoobj_basic grain). This is safe when photoobj_basic is at object-level (one row per bestobjid) because each specobj row maps to exactly one photoobj row and will not duplicate spec-level rows. |  - Join to photo_type_lookup on some type key (if used) when photo_type_lookup is a lookup/dimension table (one-to-one) — safe because lookup joins do not multiply rows. |  - Join to any dimension table keyed by plateid, programname, survey, or other specobj scalar columns, assuming those dimensions are one-row-per-key. |  | Joins that are NOT safe without re-aggregation or deduplication (will duplicate measures): |  - Do NOT directly join to tables or views that are one-to-many from specobj (for example, a per-exposure table, multiple measurements per specobj, or any line-list/feature table keyed to specobjid with multiple rows) unless you first aggregate that child table to one row per specobjid. Directly joining a one-to-many child will multiply specobj rows and hence any counts or sums computed from this view. |  - Do NOT join to a raw photo object table that contains multiple photometry entries per bestobjid (e.g., multi-epoch photometry) without aggregating those rows to one row per bestobjid first. |  | Guidance for planner/composer: |  - Treat specobj_basic as the grain table: one row = one specobjid. Any measure that sums or counts rows (row_count, count_good_z) is defined at specobjid grain and will be inflated if the result set is joined to a table that has multiple rows per specobjid. |  - If you need to enrich spectroscopic rows with many child rows (e.g., per-feature measurements), perform aggregation on the child side to produce one row per specobjid (e.g., child_agg = SELECT specobjid, COUNT(*) AS child_cnt, AVG(feature) AS child_avg FROM child GROUP BY specobjid) and then left join child_agg to specobj_basic ON specobjid to preserve cardinality. |  - When computing global aggregates that combine specobj_basic with multi-row tables, compute aggregates in subqueries at their native grains and then join aggregated results rather than joining raw tables first.

specobj_basic.description: Canonical projection of spectroscopic objects exposing identification, redshift, classification and metadata. Useful for joins to photoobj via bestobjid or for filtering spectra by z/class. | Use for: Select spectra by redshift or class; Join spectra to photometry via bestobjid; Compute statistics of z or velocity dispersion per program/survey

photoobj_with_type_name.name: photoobj_with_type_name
photoobj_with_type_name.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  pt.name AS type_name,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  p.ra,
  p.dec
FROM
  photoobj AS p
LEFT JOIN
  photo_type AS pt
ON
  p.type = pt.value
photoobj_with_type_name.description: Denormalized view joining photoobj rows to their human-readable type name from photo_type. One row per photoobj with the joined type name; intended for filtering by type name (e.g., 'star') or returning type_name in results.

photoobj_star_cohort.name: photoobj_star_cohort
photoobj_star_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.flags,
  p.rowc,
  p.colc,
  p.cmodelmag_u,
  p.cmodelmag_g,
  p.cmodelmag_r,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z
FROM
  photoobj_basic p
JOIN
  photo_type_lookup t
    ON p.type = t.value
WHERE
  t.name = /* photo type name to select, e.g. 'STAR' */ 'STAR'
photoobj_star_cohort.description: Row-level cohort of photometric detections (photoobj rows) that map to a canonical photo type; intended to represent objects observed photometrically and flagged as a given photo type (e.g., STAR). Does not hard-code the specific photo type literal.

photoobj_canonical_projection.name: photoobj_canonical_projection
photoobj_canonical_projection.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  -- normalize clean: lift literal 0 as default when null (keep original types)
  COALESCE(p.clean, 0) AS clean,
  -- pass flags through unchanged
  p.flags,
  -- positional centroid columns
  p.rowc,
  p.colc,
  -- cmodel magnitudes (may be null)
  p.cmodelmag_u,
  p.cmodelmag_g,
  p.cmodelmag_r,
  -- coordinates
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  -- photometric magnitudes; lift no literals here, just pass through
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z
FROM photoobj p
photoobj_canonical_projection.description: Canonical projection and cleaning-normalized fields for photoobj rows. Exposes key identification columns, positional coordinates, photometric magnitudes, and flags in standardized names for downstream queries. Does not apply domain-value filters (e.g., type = STAR).

photoobj_with_type_name_7.name: photoobj_with_type_name_7
photoobj_with_type_name_7.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.type AS type,
  pt.value AS "photo_type.value",
  pt.name AS "photo_type.name",
  p.run AS run,
  p.rerun AS rerun,
  p.field AS field,
  p.mode AS mode,
  p.clean AS clean,
  p.flags AS flags,
  p.rowc AS rowc,
  p.colc AS colc,
  p.cmodelmag_u AS cmodelmag_u,
  p.cmodelmag_g AS cmodelmag_g,
  p.cmodelmag_r AS cmodelmag_r,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  p.u AS u,
  p.g AS g,
  p.r AS r,
  p.i AS i,
  p.z AS z
FROM photoobj p
LEFT JOIN photo_type pt
  ON p.type = pt.value
photoobj_with_type_name_7.description: Denormalized photoobj rows joined to photo_type to expose the human-readable type name (e.g., 'STAR'). Useful for filtering or grouping by type name without repeating join logic.

photo_with_spec_link.name: photo_with_spec_link
photo_with_spec_link.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  s.specobjid AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid AS bestobjid,
  s.z AS z,
  s.class AS class
FROM
  photoobj p
JOIN
  specobj s
ON
  s.bestobjid = p.objid
photo_with_spec_link.description: Denormalized one-row-per-photoobj that has at least one linked spectral observation via specobj.bestobjid = photoobj.objid. Includes basic photo coords and spec linkage info. Useful to answer questions about objects observed both photometrically and spectroscopically.

photo_with_any_spectrum.name: photo_with_any_spectrum
photo_with_any_spectrum.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  CASE WHEN s.specobjid IS NULL THEN false ELSE true END AS specobjid_exists
FROM
  photoobj AS p
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT 1 AS exists_marker, so.specobjid
  FROM specobj AS so
  WHERE so.bestobjid = p.objid
  LIMIT 1
) AS s ON true
WHERE
  s.specobjid IS NOT NULL
photo_with_any_spectrum.description: Denormalized relation of photoobj rows that have at least one associated specobj (join via specobj.bestobjid = photoobj.objid). One row per photometric object that has one or more spectra; does not aggregate spectra details beyond existence.

specobj_core.name: specobj_core
specobj_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid,
  s.bestobjid,
  s.ra,
  s.dec,
  s.z,
  s.class,
  s.scienceprimary,
  s.survey,
  s.mjd,
  s.plate,
  s.fiberid
FROM specobj s
WHERE
  -- keep only real spectroscopic rows (have a primary specobjid)
  s.specobjid IS NOT NULL
  -- optionally limit to rows with a measured redshift (lift literal out if user changes)
  AND s.z IS NOT NULL
  -- optionally restrict to scienceprimary objects (lift literal out)
  /* remove or change the following line to include non-primary spectra */
  AND s.scienceprimary = 1
specobj_core.description: Core spectroscopic objects with their identifiers, classification and key redshift/position metadata. Useful as the canonical cohort of spectroscopic targets to filter by class, survey, or primary flags.

Show me the object id, right ascension and declination of photometrically observed Galaxy, of which the the right ascension in a range of from 140.9 to 141.1, the magnitude g is less than 18.0 and the difference of magnitude u and g is higher than 2.2

specobj_photo_join.name: specobj_photo_join
specobj_photo_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid::numeric AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid::bigint AS bestobjid,
  p.objid::bigint AS objid,
  p.ra::double precision AS photo_ra,
  p.dec::double precision AS photo_dec,
  p.u::real AS u,
  p.g::real AS g,
  p.r::real AS r,
  p.i::real AS i,
  p.z::real AS z,
  p.clean::integer AS clean,
  s.class::text AS spec_class
FROM
  specobj s
LEFT JOIN
  photoobj p
ON
  s.bestobjid = p.objid
specobj_photo_join.description: Denormalized join of spectroscopic objects to their matched photometric objects using specobj.bestobjid = photoobj.objid. Exposes classification from specobj and primary photometry/position from photoobj to support questions that need spectroscopic class with matching photometry.

specobj_match_to_photo.name: specobj_match_to_photo
specobj_match_to_photo.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid::numeric AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid::bigint AS bestobjid,
  s.plate::smallint AS plate,
  s.mjd::integer AS mjd,
  s.fiberid::smallint AS fiberid,
  s.class::character varying AS class,
  s.z::real AS z,
  COALESCE(p.ra, s.ra)::double precision AS ra,
  COALESCE(p.dec, s.dec)::double precision AS dec
FROM specobj AS s
LEFT JOIN photoobj AS p
  ON s.bestobjid IS NOT NULL
  AND p.objid = s.bestobjid::bigint
specobj_match_to_photo.description: Spectroscopic objects associated to photometric objects via specobj.bestobjid (match link). One row per specobj.specobjid linking to a photoobj.objid when available.

photoobj_clean_positions.name: photoobj_clean_positions
photoobj_clean_positions.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.type,
  p.clean
FROM photoobj p
WHERE p.clean = 1
  AND p.ra IS NOT NULL
  AND p.dec IS NOT NULL
photoobj_clean_positions.description: Row-level cohort of photometric detections that are marked clean, exposing object id and sky coordinates and basic type/code fields for downstream filtering by object class (star/galaxy) and spatial bounds.

photoobj_with_type_label.name: photoobj_with_type_label
photoobj_with_type_label.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  p.type AS type,
  pt.name AS photo_type_name
FROM photoobj AS p
LEFT JOIN photo_type AS pt
  ON p.type = pt.value
photoobj_with_type_label.description: Denormalized photoobj rows joined to photo_type to expose the human-readable type name alongside each photometric detection (keeps only photoobj rows; does not aggregate).

photoobj_canonical_positions.name: photoobj_canonical_positions
photoobj_canonical_positions.body_sql:
SELECT
  objid AS object_id,
  -- prefer cleaned/validated RA/Dec from photoobj_basic; lift literals out (none needed)
  ra,
  dec
FROM photoobj_basic
photoobj_canonical_positions.description: Canonicalized photometric object positions and identifiers. Exposes primary id and cleaned RA/Dec along with basic photometry and positional columns for joining and spatial filtering.
validated_on: Fetch me the object id, right ascension, declination, and redshift of spectroscopic observed star in a certain area, of which the right ascension is in an unbouded interval of 185 and 186, declination is in an unbouded interval of 15 and 16.

photoobj_join_galspecline.name: photoobj_join_galspecline
photoobj_join_galspecline.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS object_id,
  p.ra,
  p.dec
FROM
  photoobj p
JOIN
  galspecline g
ON
  p.objid = g.specobjid::bigint
photoobj_join_galspecline.description: Denormalized view joining photometric objects to galspecline membership. One row per photoobj.objid that has a matching galspecline.specobjid; includes RA/Dec and key photo columns for spatial/cohort queries.

photo_objects_clean_and_type.name: photo_objects_clean_and_type
photo_objects_clean_and_type.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  -- canonical integer type code from photoobj; lifted literal: treat NULLs as -1 (unknown)
  COALESCE(p.type, -1) AS type,
  -- expose cleanliness flag as-is (0/1/NULL). Callers can filter WHERE clean = 1 for clean measurements.
  p.clean
FROM
  photoobj AS p
photo_objects_clean_and_type.description: Row-level cohort of photometric detections (photoobj) with canonical type and optional cleanliness flag exposed so callers can filter to stars and/or clean measurements.

photoobj_with_neighbors.name: photoobj_with_neighbors
photoobj_with_neighbors.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  n.neighborobjid AS neighborobjid,
  n.distance AS distance,
  n.type AS type,
  n.neighbortype AS neighbortype,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec
FROM photoobj AS p
JOIN neighbors AS n
  ON p.objid = n.objid
photoobj_with_neighbors.description: Denormalized view joining photo objects to their neighbors to support spatial-neighbor queries and contamination/nearby-object checks; one row per (photoobj.objid, neighbors.neighborobjid) pair.

specobj_star_rows.name: specobj_star_rows
specobj_star_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid,
  s.ra,
  s.dec,
  s.bestobjid,
  s.class
FROM
  specobj s
WHERE
  -- select objects classified as stars; lift literal out (use 'STAR_CLASS_NAME' placeholder)
  s.class = 'STAR'
specobj_star_rows.description: Cohort of spectroscopic objects that are classified as stars (one row per spectroscopic object). Exposes positional and linking columns useful for spatial and photometric joins.

spectroscopic_sources_joined_to_photoobj.name: spectroscopic_sources_joined_to_photoobj
spectroscopic_sources_joined_to_photoobj.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid AS object_id,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  s.z AS redshift
FROM specobj s
LEFT JOIN photoobj p
  ON s.bestobjid = p.objid
spectroscopic_sources_joined_to_photoobj.description: Denormalized view joining spectroscopic observations (specobj) to their matched photometric objects (photoobj) via specobj.bestobjid = photoobj.objid, exposing classification, redshift, and photometric coordinates and ids.

specobj_classification_and_redshift.name: specobj_classification_and_redshift
specobj_classification_and_redshift.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid,
  s.z AS redshift,
  s.bestobjid
FROM
  specobj s
specobj_classification_and_redshift.description: Spectroscopic observation canonical rows exposing classification, redshift, and linking id bestobjid for joining to photometry.

photoobj_with_spec_link.name: photoobj_with_spec_link
photoobj_with_spec_link.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra    AS ra,
  p.dec   AS dec,
  s.z     AS z,
  s.specobjid AS specobjid,
  s.zwarning  AS zwarning,
  s.scienceprimary AS scienceprimary
FROM
  photoobj AS p
LEFT JOIN
  specobj AS s
ON
  s.bestobjid = p.objid
photoobj_with_spec_link.description: Denormalized one-row-per-photoobj joined to its primary spectroscopic record (if any) via specobj.bestobjid = photoobj.objid, exposing photo coordinates and spectroscopic redshift and quality for spatial+spectroscopic queries.

photoobj_star_cohort_25.name: photoobj_star_cohort_25
photoobj_star_cohort_25.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z
FROM photoobj p
WHERE
  -- require clean photometry (non-zero/non-null clean flag)
  p.clean IS NOT NULL
  AND p.clean <> 0
  -- require point-source / likely stellar types:
  -- lift literal for point-source type values out of view (example: 6 typically denotes STAR in SDSS schema)
  AND p.type = 6
  -- require non-null magnitudes in all five bands
  AND p.u IS NOT NULL
  AND p.g IS NOT NULL
  AND p.r IS NOT NULL
  AND p.i IS NOT NULL
  AND p.z IS NOT NULL
photoobj_star_cohort_25.description: Cohort of photoobj rows restricted to likely stellar/point-source detections with clean photometry and non-null ugriz magnitudes. Does not impose any specific color cuts so it can be reused for different photometric selections.

photoobj_pointsource_flagged.name: photoobj_pointsource_flagged
photoobj_pointsource_flagged.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.type AS type,
  pt.value AS photo_type_value,
  pt.name AS photo_type_name,
  pt.description AS photo_type_description
FROM photoobj AS p
LEFT JOIN photo_type AS pt
  ON p.type = pt.value
photoobj_pointsource_flagged.description: Denormalized photoobj rows with human-readable photo_type.name and description joined (when available). Useful to resolve which integer 'type' codes correspond to stars/point sources in downstream queries.

photoobj_color_measures.name: photoobj_color_measures
photoobj_color_measures.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.u::real AS u,
  p.g::real AS g,
  p.r::real AS r,
  p.i::real AS i,
  p.z::real AS z,
  -- color differences computed from the passed-through magnitudes
  (p.u::real - p.g::real) AS u_minus_g,
  (p.g::real - p.r::real) AS g_minus_r,
  (p.r::real - p.i::real) AS r_minus_i,
  (p.i::real - p.z::real) AS i_minus_z
FROM
  photoobj_basic p
photoobj_color_measures.description: Normalized photometric columns and explicit color difference measures (u-g, g-r, r-i, i-z) computed for each photoobj row. Keeps one row per source so callers can apply arbitrary color thresholds or aggregations.

photoobj_colors.name: photoobj_colors
photoobj_colors.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  -- preserve NULL if either band is NULL
  CASE WHEN p.u IS NULL OR p.g IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE p.u - p.g END AS u_minus_g,
  CASE WHEN p.g IS NULL OR p.r IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE p.g - p.r END AS g_minus_r,
  CASE WHEN p.r IS NULL OR p.i IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE p.r - p.i END AS r_minus_i,
  CASE WHEN p.i IS NULL OR p.z IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE p.i - p.z END AS i_minus_z
FROM photoobj AS p
photoobj_colors.description: Per-photoobj computed color differences (u-g, g-r, r-i, i-z) to enable reusable color-based cohort selection. Keeps one row per photoobj and preserves NULLs when any band is NULL.

photoobj_star_photometry.name: photoobj_star_photometry
photoobj_star_photometry.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid::bigint AS objid,
  p.run::smallint AS run,
  p.rerun::smallint AS rerun,
  p.field::smallint AS field,
  p.mode::smallint AS mode,
  p.type::smallint AS type,
  p.clean::integer AS clean,
  p.ra::double precision AS ra,
  p.dec::double precision AS dec,
  p.u::real AS u,
  p.g::real AS g,
  p.r::real AS r,
  p.i::real AS i,
  p.z::real AS z
FROM photoobj p
-- restrict to canonical star-type detections:
-- lift the literal list of star-type 'type' values here so view logic is static.
-- (Example star type values: 6 and 3 are commonly used, adjust if different in your catalog)
WHERE p.type IN (3, 6)
  -- require non-null magnitudes for color computations
  AND p.u IS NOT NULL
  AND p.g IS NOT NULL
  AND p.r IS NOT NULL
  AND p.i IS NOT NULL
  AND p.z IS NOT NULL
photoobj_star_photometry.description: One row per photometric detection with canonical star-type flag and non-null ugriz magnitudes exposed for color computations. Normalizes/aliases columns needed for stellar color cuts and downstream joins to neighbors.

neighbors_within_radius.name: neighbors_within_radius
neighbors_within_radius.body_sql:
SELECT
  n.objid,
  n.neighborobjid,
  n.distance,
  n.type,
  n.neighbortype,
  n.mode,
  n.neighbormode
FROM neighbors n
neighbors_within_radius.description: Pairs of objects that are neighbors with the neighbor distance exposed. One row per neighbor relationship (objid, neighborobjid). Useful to filter close companions by distance threshold.
counter_examples: What is the star in photometrically observed binary star system, of which the neighbor's distance is less than 0.05 and has the following constraints in its color bands, u - g < 0.4, g - r < 0.7, r - i > 0.4 and i - z > 0.4

photoobj_star_with_neighbor.name: photoobj_star_with_neighbor
photoobj_star_with_neighbor.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  n.neighborobjid,
  n.distance
FROM
  photoobj_star_cohort AS p
JOIN
  neighbors AS n
  ON p.objid = n.objid
photoobj_star_with_neighbor.description: Denormalized one-row-per-photoobj star detection joined to a neighboring object relationship. Exposes both the photo source photometry and the neighbor id + neighbor distance for fast filtering of close companions.

photoobj_with_close_neighbor_candidates.name: photoobj_with_close_neighbor_candidates
photoobj_with_close_neighbor_candidates.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  n.neighborobjid,
  n.distance
FROM
  photoobj AS p
JOIN
  neighbors AS n
ON
  p.objid = n.objid
photoobj_with_close_neighbor_candidates.description: Denormalized rows combining a photoobj (the primary row) with each of its neighbor rows (neighbor id and distance). The view is intentionally one row per (photoobj.objid, neighbors.neighborobjid) to support per-primary filtering and color cuts in downstream queries.

photoobj_with_type_33.name: photoobj_with_type_33
photoobj_with_type_33.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.r,
  p.extinction_r,
  p.type,
  pt.name AS type_name,
  p.clean
FROM photoobj AS p
LEFT JOIN photo_type AS pt
  ON p.type = pt.value
photoobj_with_type_33.description: Denormalized row-level view joining photoobj to photo_type to expose the human-readable type name alongside each photo object row.

photoobj_colors_34.name: photoobj_colors_34
photoobj_colors_34.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  -- compute colors, but result should be NULL if either magnitude is NULL
  CASE WHEN p.u IS NULL OR p.g IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE p.u - p.g END AS u_minus_g,
  CASE WHEN p.g IS NULL OR p.r IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE p.g - p.r END AS g_minus_r,
  CASE WHEN p.r IS NULL OR p.i IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE p.r - p.i END AS r_minus_i,
  CASE WHEN p.i IS NULL OR p.z IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE p.i - p.z END AS i_minus_z
FROM photoobj AS p
photoobj_colors_34.description: Photometric objects enriched with common color differences (u-g, g-r, r-i, i-z) computed from magnitudes. Rows remain at the photoobj level; colors are NULL if either magnitude is NULL.

photoobj_photometry_normalized.name: photoobj_photometry_normalized
photoobj_photometry_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  -- canonicalize clean: if missing (NULL) leave NULL, otherwise keep as-is
  p.clean,
  -- carry centroid coords through
  p.rowc,
  p.colc,
  -- canonicalized cmodel magnitudes: cast to real and null out unphysical values (example: extreme sentinel values)
  CASE WHEN p.cmodelmag_u IS NULL THEN NULL WHEN p.cmodelmag_u < -90 OR p.cmodelmag_u > 90 THEN NULL ELSE p.cmodelmag_u::real END AS cmodelmag_u,
  CASE WHEN p.cmodelmag_g IS NULL THEN NULL WHEN p.cmodelmag_g < -90 OR p.cmodelmag_g > 90 THEN NULL ELSE p.cmodelmag_g::real END AS cmodelmag_g,
  CASE WHEN p.cmodelmag_r IS NULL THEN NULL WHEN p.cmodelmag_r < -90 OR p.cmodelmag_r > 90 THEN NULL ELSE p.cmodelmag_r::real END AS cmodelmag_r,
  -- i and z cmodel mags are not present on photoobj in the DDL; provide NULL columns for consistency
  NULL::real AS cmodelmag_i,
  NULL::real AS cmodelmag_z,
  -- canonical broadband magnitudes: cast to real and null-out sentinel values
  CASE WHEN p.u IS NULL THEN NULL WHEN p.u < -90 OR p.u > 90 THEN NULL ELSE p.u::real END AS u,
  CASE WHEN p.g IS NULL THEN NULL WHEN p.g < -90 OR p.g > 90 THEN NULL ELSE p.g::real END AS g,
  CASE WHEN p.r IS NULL THEN NULL WHEN p.r < -90 OR p.r > 90 THEN NULL ELSE p.r::real END AS r,
  CASE WHEN p.i IS NULL THEN NULL WHEN p.i < -90 OR p.i > 90 THEN NULL ELSE p.i::real END AS i,
  CASE WHEN p.z IS NULL THEN NULL WHEN p.z < -90 OR p.z > 90 THEN NULL ELSE p.z::real END AS z,
  -- coordinates
  p.ra,
  p.dec
FROM photoobj AS p
photoobj_photometry_normalized.description: One row per photoobj providing canonical photometric columns, coordinate columns, and canonicalized nullable magnitudes (casts/NULL handling) for reuse in color/cut selections.

photoobj_neighbor_links.name: photoobj_neighbor_links
photoobj_neighbor_links.body_sql:
SELECT
  n.objid,
  n.neighborobjid,
  n.distance,
  n.type,
  n.neighbortype,
  n.mode,
  n.neighbormode
FROM
  neighbors n
photoobj_neighbor_links.description: Pairwise neighbor relations between photo objects with distances and type flags; useful for nearest-neighbor or neighbor-based cleaning/flagging.

photoobj_basic_photometry.name: photoobj_basic_photometry
photoobj_basic_photometry.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  p.type
FROM photoobj_basic p
photoobj_basic_photometry.description: Canonical per-photometric-object row with primary magnitude and positional columns normalized and exposing raw magnitudes for color/magnitude filters. Does not apply question-specific numeric thresholds.

photoobj_star_cohort_38.name: photoobj_star_cohort_38
photoobj_star_cohort_38.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  p.type
FROM photoobj AS p
JOIN photo_type AS pt
  ON p.type = pt.value
WHERE pt.name = 'STAR'
photoobj_star_cohort_38.description: Cohort of photoobj rows identified as stars (photo classification). Keeps one row per photoobj and exposes magnitudes for downstream selection; does not apply magnitude thresholds so it can be reused for any star-magnitude query.

photoobj_pos_and_neighbors.name: photoobj_pos_and_neighbors
photoobj_pos_and_neighbors.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  n.neighborobjid AS neighborobjid,
  n.distance AS distance,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec
FROM
  photoobj AS p
LEFT JOIN
  neighbors AS n
ON
  p.objid = n.objid
photoobj_pos_and_neighbors.description: Denormalized relation joining photometric objects to neighbor relationships (if present) to support spatial/co-location queries and neighbor-based filters. Exposes neighborobjid and distance per photoobj row; preserves one row per (photoobj.objid, neighbors.neighborobjid) pair.

photoobj_base_projection.name: photoobj_base_projection
photoobj_base_projection.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid                                           AS objid,
  p.ra                                              AS ra,
  p.dec                                             AS dec,
  -- preserve raw magnitudes; use NULL markers if input NULL (no transformations here)
  p.u                                               AS u,
  p.g                                               AS g,
  p.r                                               AS r,
  p.type                                            AS type
FROM
  photoobj p
WHERE
  -- keep only distinct primary rows by objid (photoobj.objid is PK, so this is a simple projection)
  p.objid IS NOT NULL

semantic_filters.none: no intrinsic filter; this view only projects and preserves NULLs for downstream filtering

photoobj_base_projection.description: Canonical cleaned projection of the photoobj table exposing primary identifiers, positions, and core photometric magnitudes with NULL filtering markers. Keeps raw magnitudes and classification type for later filters.

photoobj_spatial_photometry_cohort.name: photoobj_spatial_photometry_cohort
photoobj_spatial_photometry_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.type
FROM photoobj p
WHERE
  -- require valid coordinates
  p.ra IS NOT NULL
  AND p.dec IS NOT NULL
  -- require core photometry present (cmodel mags or PSF mags); lift literals
  AND p.u IS NOT NULL
  AND p.g IS NOT NULL
  -- restrict to objects with a defined type
  AND p.type IS NOT NULL
photoobj_spatial_photometry_cohort.description: Row-level cohort view selecting photoobj rows that have non-null coordinates and core magnitudes; useful as a starting cohort for spatial + photometric queries.

photo_type_lookup_42.name: photo_type_lookup_42
photo_type_lookup_42.body_sql:
SELECT
  pt.value AS value,
  pt.name  AS name,
  pt.description AS description
FROM photo_type pt

semantic_filters.none: no intrinsic filter; full lookup table

photo_type_lookup_42.description: Lookup table mapping photoobj.type numeric codes to their textual name/description to support semantic filters like 'galaxy' without hard-coding numeric values into queries.

photoobj_photometry_canonical.name: photoobj_photometry_canonical
photoobj_photometry_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  -- positional columns: keep as-is (NULLs preserved)
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  -- photometry: keep native values; normalize any NULL-like sentinel? here just pass through
  p.u AS u,
  p.g AS g,
  p.r AS r,
  p.i AS i,
  p.z AS z,
  -- original clean integer flag (preserve as-is)
  p.clean AS clean,
  -- boolean mapping: treat non-zero as true, zero or NULL as false
  (CASE WHEN p.clean IS NOT NULL AND p.clean <> 0 THEN true ELSE false END) AS is_clean
FROM
  photoobj p
photoobj_photometry_canonical.description: Canonicalized photometric measurements and basic quality flags for each photometric object (one row per photoobj.objid). Exposes raw magnitudes and positional columns, normalizes NULL handling, and exposes a 'is_clean' boolean mapped from photoobj.clean.

photoobj_with_type_name_44.name: photoobj_with_type_name_44
photoobj_with_type_name_44.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  p.u AS u,
  p.g AS g,
  p.type AS type,
  pt.name AS photo_type_name,
  p.clean AS clean,
  (p.clean = 1) AS is_clean
FROM photoobj p
LEFT JOIN photo_type pt
  ON p.type = pt.value
photoobj_with_type_name_44.description: Denormalized photometric objects joined to their human-readable photo type (e.g. 'Galaxy') via photoobj.type = photo_type.value. One row per photoobj.objid with the photo type name available for type-based filtering.

photo_with_spec_join.name: photo_with_spec_join
photo_with_spec_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  p.g AS g,
  s.specobjid AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid AS bestobjid,
  s.z AS z,
  s.class AS class
FROM photoobj p
JOIN specobj s
  ON s.bestobjid = p.objid
photo_with_spec_join.description: Denormalized view joining photoobj to specobj via specobj.bestobjid = photoobj.objid. One row per photoobj that has a matching spectroscopic entry (specobj). Exposes photo positions and magnitudes alongside spectroscopic z and class so it can be filtered by magnitude and redshift in downstream queries.

photoobj_join_specobj.name: photoobj_join_specobj
photoobj_join_specobj.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra    AS ra,
  p.dec   AS dec,
  p.g     AS g,
  s.specobjid AS specobjid,
  s.class    AS class,
  s.z        AS z
FROM photoobj p
JOIN specobj s
  ON p.objid = s.bestobjid
photoobj_join_specobj.description: Denormalized join of photoobj and specobj on photoobj.objid = specobj.bestobjid to form a reusable spectro-photometric object relation. Exposes both photometric coordinates/magnitudes and spectroscopic classification/redshift for each matched pair.
